constraints: left-to-right chains of two operations; exact quotients
hints: Identify operation order and confirm each divisor is nonzero.
Perform multiplication and division strictly left to right, using each intermediate signed result.
Check an intermediate quotient by inverse multiplication before continuing.

constraints: absolute value evaluated before outside operations
hints: Mark grouping, absolute value, and multiplication or division before addition or subtraction.
Evaluate each grouped signed expression, treating absolute value as distance before outside operations.
Continue by priority and check that every subtraction kept its sign.

objective: Order a mixed list of rationals
constraints: three or four values mixing fractions and decimals; denominators up to 10
hints: Convert values to comparable forms or locate them on a number line.
For negatives, the value with the greater magnitude lies farther left and is smaller.
Order from left to right and check each adjacent comparison.

objective: Signed fractions where one denominator divides the other
constraints: one denominator divides the other; denominators up to 12
hints: Rewrite any subtraction as adding the opposite, then find a common denominator.
Rewrite both fractions with equal-sized parts and combine signed numerators.
Reduce the result and check its sign against the magnitudes.

constraints: denominators up to 12; answers in lowest terms
hints: Identify multiplication or division and the signs.
For division multiply by the reciprocal of the nonzero second fraction; then multiply numerators and denominators with cancellation.
Reduce and check sign with inverse operation.

constraints: convert to one form first; denominators up to 10
hints: Convert every decimal or fraction to one exact form before choosing an operation.

For sums use a common denominator and combine signed numerators; for products multiply numerator with numerator and denominator with denominator; for division reverse the second fraction then multiply.
Simplify and check the sign using the rule for that operation, especially for sums and differences.

constraints: convert to improper fractions first; denominators up to 12
hints: Convert each mixed-number magnitude to an improper fraction and keep its leading sign on the whole quantity.
Rewrite subtraction as addition of the opposite and use a common denominator.
Combine signed numerators, reduce, and estimate against the original signed magnitudes.
